strategies.title: EMA cross baseline
strategies.summary: Minimal EMA crossover used as the platform baseline.
strategies.description: A deliberately small trend strategy: it enters when the fast EMA crosses above the slow EMA and exits on the opposite cross. It carries no filters, no stop-loss tuning and no pair specific parameters, which makes it the reference every other strategy is measured against. Because it reacts to every cross, it is expected to lose money in ranging markets.
strategies.risk_notes: Whipsaws in ranging markets; the only exit is the opposite cross, so drawdowns can run.

strategies.title: Momentum breakout
strategies.summary: Buys strength while price momentum stays positive and above its trend filter.
strategies.description: The strategy measures the rate of change of the close over a short lookback and only trades in the direction of that momentum. A longer EMA acts as a regime filter so that long entries are taken in uptrends and short entries in downtrends. Momentum decays quickly in crypto, so positions are closed as soon as the reading flips sign.
strategies.risk_notes: Momentum crashes: it enters late in an extended move and gives back gains on a sharp reversal.

strategies.title: RSI mean reversion
strategies.summary: Fades oversold RSI readings inside a longer term uptrend.
strategies.description: Entries are taken when RSI drops below the oversold threshold while price is still above its long EMA, which keeps the strategy on the right side of the main trend. The position is closed once RSI recovers to the neutral band. It deliberately avoids shorting, so it only earns in markets that mean revert upwards.
strategies.reference: Relative Strength Index, J. Welles Wilder (1978) - https://www.investopedia.com/terms/r/rsi.asp
strategies.risk_notes: A persistent downtrend keeps RSI oversold while price keeps falling; no short leg to hedge it.

strategies.title: Bollinger band reversion
strategies.summary: Buys the lower Bollinger band touch and exits at the middle band.
strategies.description: The strategy treats a close below the lower Bollinger band as a stretched move and buys the reversion towards the moving average. RSI is used as a second confirmation so that entries only happen when the move is genuinely oversold. The exit is the middle band, which keeps the holding period short and the trade count high.
strategies.risk_notes: Bands widen with volatility, so a breakout trend can keep price outside the band for a long time.

strategies.title: MACD trend follow
strategies.summary: Trades MACD crossovers filtered by the long EMA regime.
strategies.description: A classic MACD crossover provides the entry timing, with the histogram turning positive as confirmation. The long EMA decides whether the platform is allowed to be long at all, which removes most counter trend signals. Exits happen when the MACD line crosses back below its signal line.
strategies.risk_notes: MACD lags by construction: entries arrive after a large part of the move and exits after the top.

strategies.title: Donchian channel breakout
strategies.summary: Buys a new twenty period high and exits on the opposite channel.
strategies.description: The strategy is a turtle style breakout: a close above the upper Donchian channel opens a long position and a close below the lower channel closes it. ATR is used to size the position in risk terms rather than in notional terms. It is designed for strongly trending markets and trades rarely.
strategies.risk_notes: Breakouts fail often in ranges, producing a string of small losses before a trend appears.

strategies.title: Keltner channel breakout
strategies.summary: Trades volatility adjusted breakouts of the Keltner channel.
strategies.description: The Keltner channel is built from an EMA and ATR, which makes it smoother than a Bollinger band and less sensitive to single candle spikes. A close above the upper band opens a long position while the EMA slope confirms the direction. The exit is the channel midline, so profits are taken before the trend fully reverses.
strategies.risk_notes: Low volatility compresses the channel and produces frequent, low quality breakouts.

strategies.title: Supertrend trailing stop
strategies.summary: Follows the Supertrend direction with an ATR trailing stop.
strategies.description: The Supertrend indicator flips between an upper and a lower ATR band; the strategy is long while price holds above the band and flat otherwise. The band doubles as a trailing stop, which caps the loss of a failed entry without a fixed target. An EMA filter avoids taking long signals in a clear downtrend.
strategies.risk_notes: The ATR multiplier sets the trade frequency: too tight and it whipsaws, too wide and stops are expensive.

strategies.title: Dual Thrust range breakout
strategies.summary: Intraday range breakout built from the previous range and two thrust factors.
strategies.description: Dual Thrust computes an upper and a lower trigger from the previous session range and two independent thrust factors. A break of either trigger opens a position in that direction, and the opposite trigger closes it. The asymmetric factors make the strategy react faster to upside breaks than to downside ones.
strategies.reference: Dual Thrust range breakout, Michael Chalek - https://bigquant.com/wiki/doc/celve-9zCGg7j7az
strategies.risk_notes: Sensitive to the session boundary used for the range; false breaks inside a range are the main cost.

strategies.title: Faber trend allocation
strategies.summary: Holds the asset only while it trades above its long moving average.
strategies.description: This is Mebane Faber's tactical asset allocation rule applied to a single pair: hold the asset when the close is above its two hundred period moving average, and stay in cash otherwise. It trades a handful of times per year and exists to give the platform a low turnover, low drawdown allocation profile. It is intentionally the slowest strategy of the catalogue.
strategies.reference: Mebane Faber, A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation (2007) - https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=962461
strategies.risk_notes: Wide, slow signals: it gives back a large part of a move before the average is crossed.
